message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• In cities: 25–35 mph.
• School zones: 20 mph (or 25 mph if posted). | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Lower BAC limits for commercial drivers and drivers under 21. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.
• At uncontrolled intersections, yield to traffic coming from the right. | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Fog lights are allowed only when visibility is ≤ 200 ft. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display valid registration stickers.
• Towing laws require a proper tow bar and safe towing practices. | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, driveways, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | | **School Bus** | • Stop on both sides of the road when a school bus is loading/unloading children. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing.
• Use turn signals at least 100 ft before turning. | | **Traffic Cameras & Speed Cameras** | • Texas uses speed cameras in some counties; fines are issued automatically. | | **Insurance** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 bodily injury per person, $60,000 per accident, $25,000 property damage. | ### Where to Find the Full Text - **Texas Transportation Code** – Chapter 545 (Traffic Rules) and Chapter 546 (Traffic Regulations). - **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – provides downloadable PDFs and interactive maps. - **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** – offers driver’s handbook and licensing information. ### Quick Tips for Drivers 1. **Always obey posted signs** – they’re the law. 2. **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk on the phone. 3. **Check your vehicle’s registration** before you hit the road. 4. **Keep a safe following distance** – at least one car length per 10 mph. 5. **Stay alert for pedestrians and cyclists** – especially in urban areas. If you need more detailed information on a specific aspect (e.g., DUI penalties, toll roads, or commercial driving regulations), let me know!
